comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide study BA-KOR and its public product API identify 60 EC in each year. The chosen coherent pathway selects one permitted first-year 5-EC methods course and one 5-EC regional course; Korean 3 (15 EC) rather than the alternative Korea study-language component; Themes and Approaches (10 EC) rather than Hanmun; two of the five 5-EC second-year subject electives; Intermediate Korean Reading 2A; one third-year language course and one 10-EC topical seminar. The 10-EC BA Final paper and 5-EC seminar are compulsory. Thirty EC of genuinely open third-year elective space are preserved as two 15-EC components. The 0-EC mentorship and non-curricular group are excluded. The adopted OER confirms no formal graduation tracks and the Korean-language prerequisites. Current module EC and the selected study groups were checked on 2026-09-26 and sum to 180 EC.

exception.reason: Leiden’s Korean Studies bachelor integrates a cumulative Korean-language sequence with Korean history, thought, culture, society, politics and region-specific methods. The chosen 180-EC pathway includes 65 EC of dedicated Korean-language and Korean-reading courses before the thesis (Korean 1–3, Korean Language in Use, Intermediate Korean Reading 1 and 2A, and Business Korean), and further Korean-centred seminars and primary-source work. UCR has no Korean-language course and no Korea-specific history, media, literature or politics course. A curriculum of 24 UCR courses drawn from broadly related social sciences and humanities would fail the requirement that each non-PPD course contribute concretely to the target-specific concept. It would conceal the central language and Korea-based source-training gap, so no defensible closest UCR alternative can be constructed.
exception.curriculumContext: The 2026–27 official catalogue shows first year 50 EC compulsory plus two 5-EC restricted choices; second year 20 EC compulsory and 40 EC specified restricted choices; third year a 5-EC compulsory thesis seminar, 15 EC of restricted language/topic study, a 10-EC final paper and 30 EC of free elective space. A single coherent option was selected in each restricted group. The programme-specific adopted OER confirms language progression from Korean 1 through Korean 3, further reading and final source-based work. No formal graduation route is named. All 180 EC are accounted for exactly once.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. No UCR course teaches Korean or specifically covers either Korea, Korean cultural sources or Korean history. GOSHIST111/211/312 cover modern history, empires and historical research without the Korean sequence; GOSPOLI112/212/313 address comparative politics, international relations and conflict without Korea-specific material. MCCMEDI111/211, MCCLITR111/311 and MCCHEAM111 can teach media, literature and art methods, but not Korean-language source reading or the Korea-centred historical and cultural curriculum. HCBCOGN312 examines psycholinguistics rather than Korean language acquisition. Those neighbouring methods do not sustain 23 substantively relevant non-PPD courses for a Korean Studies concept; semester feasibility cannot cure the subject mismatch.
